### A Plymouth showroom where your new kitchen gets planned
MJ Kitchen & Bath handles kitchen remodeling in Plymouth from the first sketch to the last cabinet pull. The company began in 2009 as MJ Cabinet Designs, building custom kitchens for local builders, then added full remodeling for homeowners and took its current name in December 2019.

In June 2026 the team opened a larger showroom at 620 Ann Arbor Road, just across the street from the old one. Inside are kitchen and bath displays of Wood-Mode, Showplace and Pioneer cabinets, plus a selection center for tile, quartz and granite, flooring and hardware, so you can compare finishes side by side before you commit.

### Kitchen remodeling in Plymouth and the rooms around it
- **Kitchen remodeling**: The team designs and installs the whole kitchen: cabinets, counters, tile, sinks, lighting and flooring. You see floor plans, elevation drawings and color renderings before work starts, and MJ's own cost guide puts same-layout kitchen remodels at $50,000 and up.
- **Bathroom remodeling**: Primary baths, powder rooms, Jack-and-Jill layouts and busy family bathrooms. Popular requests include curbless walk-in showers, freestanding soaking tubs, radiant-heat floors and vanities with pull-out storage. MJ says most bath remodels are finished in 3 to 6 weeks.
- **Semi-custom and custom cabinetry**: Choose from Wood-Mode, crafted in Pennsylvania, Showplace from South Dakota and Pioneer from Michigan. Beyond kitchens, MJ builds cabinets for laundry rooms, mudrooms, wet bars, coffee bars and home offices, and its own carpenters install what it sells.
- **First-floor remodels**: For bigger plans, MJ redesigns the first floor around a larger kitchen, with possible structural changes, fine custom cabinetry and new hardwood throughout. These projects start at $150,000 and often add a wet or dry bar, a powder room refresh or a new fireplace mantel.

### Why Plymouth homeowners keep calling MJ back
- **One family, two generations**: Mike Jenkins has worked in cabinetry for more than 30 years and founded the company. Matt Jenkins leads remodeling sales, and Ryan Jenkins is one of the lead carpenters.
- **Clients come back for the next room**: Rebecca A. hired MJ for her kitchen, then brought the same team back for two bathrooms the following year and for the last bathroom after that.
- **A project manager on every job**: Your designated project manager and crew seal off nearby rooms to cut dust, clean up every day and finish with a punch list before they call the job done.
- **Ranked with the nation's largest**: Qualified Remodeler ranked MJ 394th in its 2026 Top 500, one of only 32 kitchen and bath firms on the list. Matt was also a finalist for the 2025 Fred Case Award.

### From MJ Cabinet Designs to MJ Kitchen & Bath
Mike Jenkins spent more than 30 years in the cabinetry trade before opening MJ Cabinet Designs in 2009, building luxury custom kitchens and baths with local builders. As homeowners asked for more, the company added start-to-finish remodeling and became MJ Kitchen & Bath in December 2019. Today Mike (Owner, Cabinet Sales) and his fellow owner Matt Jenkins (Owner, Remodeling Sales) run it as a two-generation family business, with in-house designers, a project manager and lead carpenters. ### Five steps from first call to final punch list
1. **Quick inquiry and ballpark**: Fill out the short inquiry form and the team calls back to review your project, give an initial ballpark estimate and outline next steps.
2. **In-home consultation**: A team member visits to take exact measurements, listen to your wish list and share layout ideas that make the most of the space.

4. **Selections with an interior designer**: Pick cabinets, counters, backsplash, flooring and hardware from showroom samples, then see your choices in color renderings before anything is ordered.
5. **Construction and wrap-up**: MJ secures permits and orders materials, then your project manager and crew build it, clean up daily and close out a punch list.

### Questions Plymouth homeowners ask before they remodel
- **How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Plymouth?** MJ's own cost guide, based on its projects in Plymouth, Northville, Canton, Ann Arbor and Livonia, lists three levels. Same-layout remodels start at $50,000, expanded remodels with wall removal start at $100,000, and first-floor remodels start at $150,000. Final cost depends on cabinet line, layout changes, material choices and the age of the home.
- **How long will my kitchen or bathroom be under construction?** MJ estimates 6 weeks or more of construction for a same-layout kitchen and 8 weeks or more for larger kitchen projects, counted from the start of construction. Most bathroom remodels take 3 to 6 weeks. Design, selections and ordering are all completed before construction begins, though permits or material lead times can shift dates.
- **Can I see cabinets in person before I choose?** Yes. The showroom at 620 Ann Arbor Road has kitchen and bath displays of Wood-Mode, Showplace and Pioneer cabinetry, plus samples of tile, quartz and granite, flooring and hardware. Appointments are preferred, Saturday visits are by appointment, and customer parking is in front and along the west side of the building.
- **Do you handle design, or do I need my own designer?** MJ has its own design team. After an in-home measure you receive floor plans, elevation drawings and a written estimate, then you work with an interior designer on finishes and get color renderings of your selections. If you already have an interior designer or builder, MJ works with them too.
- **Will you take on a bathroom-only project?** Yes. The team remodels primary baths, guest and powder rooms, Jack-and-Jill layouts and high-traffic family bathrooms. Features it installs include curbless walk-in showers with Euro-style glass doors, freestanding soaking tubs, radiant-heat floors, built-in benches and vanities with pull-out storage for hair tools.

### What to know before you finish a basement or remodel
- **How much does a finished basement cost?** Majestic publishes three packages for qualifying homes built in 1985 or later: Bronze at $65,000 for 750 to 850 square feet, Silver at $85,000 for 850 to 1,000 square feet, and Gold at $100,000 for 1,000 to 1,100 square feet. ### You see the real cost of every fixture
Ann Arbor Remodeling is a full-service firm for design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, taking on everything from bathroom renovations to complete home remodels and additions. Every project is designed from scratch, and the team handles the first design concept, permits and construction all the way through final inspection.

Pricing works differently here. Instead of hiding markups in line items, the contract shows what the company pays its trade partners and the direct cost of your finish materials. If a toilet costs them $478, that is the number you see. Owner Justin Kolic wants the company on the same side of the table as its clients.

### Design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, from kitchens to additions
- **Kitchen remodeling**: Custom kitchens planned around how your family cooks, with cabinetry design, material selections and lighting layouts worked out with your designer. The company's directional pricing puts a medium-size kitchen remodel with mid-level finishes at $125k to $175k.
- **Bathroom remodeling**: Primary suites and hall baths, built by a lead carpenter who stays on your job until it is finished. The newest finished project, the Huron River Primary Suite, pairs a freestanding tub with wood-look tile. Hall bathroom projects are listed at $50k to $55k.
- **Basement finishing**: Basements fall under the Lead Carpenter System, so the same person is on site each weekday, coordinating trade partners and inspectors. On the company's pricing guide, a 1500-square-foot basement with a bathroom and bar starts at $200k.
- **Additions, sunrooms and screen porches**: Additions begin with a discovery day at your home, opening drywall to confirm conditions so the schedule holds. The team also builds sunrooms and screen porches that connect indoors and out. A 200-square-foot kitchen addition starts at $300k.
- **Custom woodworking**: With its own wood shop and carpenters, the company builds bookcases, fireplace built-ins and mantels, built-in cabinetry and even custom tables, so the storage, shelving and trim in your remodel are made for that exact room.

### How Justin's team runs a job
- **Transparent contracts**: Your contract lists what the company pays trade partners and the direct cost of your finishes, with no hidden markups tucked into the line items.
- **One lead carpenter, one project**: On kitchens, baths and basements, a hands-on lead carpenter manages only your job and is typically on site from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.
- **Daily logs you can check**: Daily logs, progress photos and change orders post to BuilderTrend, so you know where things stand even if you are across the country.
- **Cleaner air while you live there**: Crews set up zip walls and air scrubbers to limit dust and contaminants, which matters when your family stays home during construction.

### A future teacher who chose the trades
Justin Kolic decided to become a remodeler in 2003 while studying to be a teacher. He finished an associate degree, took construction management classes at WCC and earned his Michigan Residential Builders license in 2006. He started Ann Arbor Remodeling LLC in 2013. 3. **Pre-construction**: You review the contract, plans and final scope, permits are applied for, and you meet the project manager who will run your job.
4. **Construction**: Your project manager shares progress, schedule and changes in Buildertrend and holds milestone meetings, and your designer returns for paint, tile and cabinet install reviews.

### Condo remodeling in Chicago, planned around your building's rules
Condo remodeling in Chicago is mostly about the building. Before a wall comes down there is an alteration agreement, insurance certificates, elevator bookings and work-hour rules. Assembly Squad has handled that paperwork since 2013, and today 75% of its completed projects are condominium renovations.

The firm is a licensed design-build general contractor, so one team covers design, permits, materials, construction and the final walkthrough. You meet your designer at the Lincoln Park studio, pick real materials, and get a fixed-price proposal. Then a dedicated project manager runs the job and sends daily photo updates while you get on with your week.

### What we renovate in Chicago homes and condos
- **Condo Remodeling**: Gut renovations and single-room updates in high-rises, lofts and greystone conversions. The team prepares alteration agreements, insurance certificates, drawings, neighbor notices and board presentations, then works within building hours. Typical condo budgets run $25,000 to $250,000+, depending on scope.
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Custom cabinetry, quartz countertops, new appliances and full layout changes for condos, two-flats and single-family homes. Kitchens are the firm's most requested service, with typical budgets from $25,000 to $150,000+. You see 3D renderings and choose every material before construction starts.
- **Bathroom Renovation**: Walk-in shower conversions, custom vanities, heated floors and tile work designed around condo plumbing stacks and building waterproofing rules. Bathroom budgets typically run $15,000 to $55,000. Recent work includes lofts in the West Loop and high-rise units in Lakeshore East.
- **Basement Finishing**: Family rooms, home offices, wet bars, ADUs and legal rental units, with waterproofing included in the scope. Typical basement budgets run $30,000 to $100,000+. Permits and inspections are part of every project, so you are not left dealing with the city alone.
- **Whole Home Renovation**: Complete gut rehabs covering the kitchen, every bathroom, flooring, plumbing and electrical. The team works on Chicago greystones, vintage two-flats, single-family homes and condo conversions, and as an EPA Lead-Safe Certified Firm it can work in pre-1978 homes. Typical budgets start around $85,000.
- **Illinois-Made Custom Cabinets**: Since 2024 the firm has offered Illinois-made custom cabinetry for kitchens, baths and built-ins. Lead times run 4 to 6 weeks instead of the 16 weeks the firm saw on imports, with no tariff exposure. Full-size displays are open to see at the Lincoln Park studio.

### Why condo owners choose Assembly Squad
- **300+ buildings already approved**: The firm is pre-approved in more than 300 Chicago buildings and reports zero HOA complaints in 13 years. Alteration agreements, insurance certificates and elevator scheduling are part of every condo job.
- **A fixed price before anything is ordered**: You get a detailed estimate within 48 hours and a fixed-price proposal after design. If you ask for a change mid-project, it is priced and signed in writing first.
- **See it at the Lincoln Park studio**: The 2,500 sq ft showroom at 2315 N Southport Ave holds 500+ cabinet, countertop, tile, hardware and flooring samples, plus free 3D renderings of your project.
- **Licensed, insured and warrantied**: License #TGC098779, $2M liability insurance, an A+ BBB rating and a 2-year written workmanship warranty on all Assembly Squad labor.

### Founded by Viktor Aharon after 22+ years in remodeling
Viktor Aharon spent more than 22 years in remodeling watching homeowners juggle contractors, chase permit updates and make decisions nobody prepared them for. In 2011 he built the first Assembly Squad as an app to help people plan and manage a renovation. By 2013 it had become a design-build general contracting company with one rule: one team, one contract, one fixed price. Viktor asks whether you are building a forever home or planning a five or six year stay, then plans the work to balance daily enjoyment with resale value.

(Viktor Aharon, Founder & CEO)

### Four steps, about twelve weeks
1. **Week 1: Free consultation**: The team visits your home or condo, reviews building requirements and talks through your plans. A detailed estimate follows within 48 hours, in person or virtual.
2. **Weeks 2 to 4: Design and approvals**: 3D renderings, material picks at the Lincoln Park studio and a fixed-price proposal, while the firm handles HOA paperwork, permits and landmark approvals.
3. **Weeks 4 to 12: Construction**: Crews work within building hours, coordinate elevators and keep the site clean. Your project manager sends daily photo updates.
4. **Final week: Walkthrough**: A punch-list inspection, touch-ups and your warranty paperwork, including the 2-year workmanship warranty on all Assembly Squad labor.

### Chicago condo remodeling questions, answered
- **Who deals with my condo board and building management?** Assembly Squad does. - **How long will my renovation take?** The standard plan runs about twelve weeks. Week one is the consultation and estimate, weeks two to four cover design, HOA paperwork and permits, and construction runs from week four to week twelve. - **Do you work outside the city?** Yes. Since 2025 the firm has brought the same design-build service to the North Shore, including Winnetka, Lake Forest, Highland Park, Glencoe and Evanston. - **Rekindle Remove-and-Replace**: Made for kitchens and baths whose layout already works. Rekindle keeps walls, plumbing and electrical where they are and replaces cabinetry, countertops, tile, flooring, lighting and fixtures. - **Whole-Home and Historic Remodels**: When a first floor needs real change, the Reimagine service removes or moves walls, adds rooms and relocates plumbing and electrical. ### Four phases, each with a timeframe you can plan around
1. **Discovery (about 1 to 2 weeks)**: A home visit to talk through your ideas, their benefits and challenges, ending with a well-reasoned view of what is possible and an approximate budget.
2. **Design (about 1 to 2 months)**: Under a design agreement, the team measures your home, tests layouts in 3D software and delivers a detailed proposal with a fixed-price contract.
3. **Refinement (about 1 to 2 months)**: Design and selection meetings with the interior designers settle wood finishes, cabinetry, fixtures, paint, tile and flooring until every element is chosen.

Your written Project Plan states the start date and expected duration, and because every selection is made before construction, the crew is not held up waiting on choices.
- **When is the best time of year to start?** The best time is whenever the work disrupts your life the least. Winter suits interior jobs like kitchens and baths because they do not depend on weather. For an addition, spring or late summer into fall works well. - **Where do I pick out cabinets, tile and fixtures?** A designer walks you through selections in the ALL showroom, at a vendor's showroom or in your home. ### A Greater Madison design-build firm that starts by listening
Degnan Design-Build-Remodel has offered kitchen remodeling in Madison, WI and the towns around it since Bob Degnan founded the company in 1981. His son Abe grew up on job sites as a helper and carpenter, then earned an architecture degree and brought a design-first approach to the family business.

Today the same team designs, prices and builds each project. A designer draws several concepts, then 3D drawings, before anyone swings a hammer. A lead carpenter runs the site once work starts. In GuildQuality surveys, 95% of clients say they would recommend the firm and 98% call the team professional and organized.

### Kitchen remodeling in Madison, WI, and the rest of the house
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: From open-concept kitchens for entertaining to efficient updates and kitchen additions. Recent projects include a kitchen with laundry in Lodi, a dual-island kitchen in DeForest and a 1970s kitchen reworked for a retired couple. Most kitchen builds take about 2 to 3 months.
- **Master Suite and Bathroom Remodeling**: Primary suites, steam showers, soaking tubs, powder rooms and tub-to-shower conversions. The team has remodeled baths in Wexford Village, Maple Bluff, Waunakee and East Madison. Plan on about 1.5 to 2.5 months of construction for a bathroom.
- **Aging-in-Place Remodeling**: Abe Degnan holds the CAPS designation for aging-in-place work. The portfolio shows curbless showers, grab bars and open kitchens planned for later years, including an affordable aging-in-place bath in Brooklyn, WI and a contemporary one in Maple Bluff.
- **Finished Basements**: Degnan calls it a finished lower level, because it should look and feel like the rest of the house. Past projects include media rooms, a wet bar, an exercise room and a lower-level living room in Oregon, WI. Basement builds usually run about 2 to 3 months.
- **Condominium Remodeling**: Condo work means HOA approval, building rules and shared walls. Degnan has remodeled units in Metropolitan Place, Weston Place, Hawks Reserve, Nolen Shores and The Marina Condominiums, plus a transitional condo kitchen and mudroom in Middleton.

### What sets the Degnan team apart
- **Two generations, one family name**: Bob Degnan started the company in 1981. His son Abe now leads it as president and Director of Design, and Zach Degnan works on the design team.
- **Scores you can check**: Independent GuildQuality surveys show 95% of clients likely to recommend Degnan, 96% satisfied with communication and 98% who felt the team was professional and organized.
- **Award-winning work**: Wins include Wisconsin Builders Association Builder of the Year in 2024 and NARI Madison Contractor of the Year for a residential kitchen under $100K in 2023.
- **They come back after the job**: You get lien paperwork, product manuals and warranties at the end. The team also checks in at 6 months and 1 year to catch any warranty work.

### Meet Abe Degnan, president and Director of Design
Abe Degnan learned the trade as a helper and carpenter in his father's company. After earning an architecture degree from UW-Milwaukee, he brought a design-first approach to the firm Bob Degnan founded in 1981. Abe now leads the team as president and Director of Design, mentors the designers and runs day-to-day operations. He holds the CGR, CGB and CAPS designations. His stated goal for every job is that it finishes on time, on budget and more beautiful than you imagined. Abe is also a proud father of six.

(Abe Degnan, President and Director of Design)

### Nine steps, three phases: how a Degnan project runs
1. **A first conversation**: A free call about your project, your goals and a ballpark budget. Photos of your space help the team give you a useful range.
2. **Design**: After a consultation and budgeting meeting, a designer measures, sketches several concepts and develops the best one into 3D drawings.
3. **Selections and estimating**: Your designer goes with you to showrooms. Trade partners walk your home so the estimate is accurate and change orders stay rare.
4. **Contract and preparation**: You sign a contract with agreed start and finish dates. Degnan pulls permits, places orders and hands the job to your lead carpenter.
5. **Build and follow-through**: The crew protects your home and controls dust. After a final walk-through, the team checks in at 6 months and 1 year.

### Design-build remodeling in Madison, WI, the Sweeney Way
Sweeney Design Remodel has offered design-build remodeling in Madison, WI since 1954. One team handles the design, the budget and the construction of kitchens, baths, basements and additions, so the people who draw your plans also answer for how they get built.

The difference is timing. Before a contract is written, Sweeney brings its plumbers, electricians and HVAC partners through your home, so problems show up on paper instead of behind your walls. Most of those trade partners have worked with Sweeney for 25 years or more, and when you refer a friend, the same people show up at their house.

### Kitchens, baths, basements and additions for Dane County homes
- **Kitchen Remodels**: Reworked layouts, opened walls, custom cabinetry, quartz or natural stone tops and layered lighting, plus the panel, plumbing and venting updates behind them. Sweeney kitchens won a NARI Contractor of the Year award in 2006 and a Chrysalis Award in 2005, both in the over-$100,000 class.
- **Bathroom Remodels**: Primary baths that feel cramped often need a smarter layout more than more square feet. Sweeney reworks the flow, builds roomier walk-in showers or soaking-tub retreats, adds vanity storage and sometimes borrows space from a closet next door. Its baths earned NARI Contractor of the Year awards in 2004 and 2013.
- **Basement Remodels**: Unfinished or dated lower levels become rec rooms, wet bars, studies, laundry and storage. Sweeney won NARI Contractor of the Year for a basement over $100,000 in 2017, and one Madison client said friends touring her finished basement could not believe it was the same house.
- **Home Additions and Whole-Home Remodels**: Additions and whole-house projects are where one accountable team matters most, because structure, permits, mechanicals and finishes all have to fit together. Sweeney took NARI Contractor of the Year for additions over $250,000 in 2005, 2006 and 2019, and for an entire house in 2017.
- **Condo Kitchens and Baths**: Condo work means tight galley or peninsula layouts and careful crews in shared buildings. Sweeney has remodeled complete Madison condos, and the president of the Marina Condo Owners Association wrote that the crew protected both his unit and the common areas while keeping residents informed.

### Why Dane County homeowners call Sweeney back
- **Trades in your home during design**: Plumbers, electricians and HVAC partners walk your home with the designers before pricing is final. Most have worked with Sweeney for 25+ years and must be licensed, insured and on time.
- **Budgets built from real history**: A Comparative Remodeling Analysis breaks your budget into line items using Sweeney's own past project costs. One client wrote that the price looked higher at first but already covered the unexpected details.
- **Certified people on the job**: Tim Sweeney and Rich Deegan are NARI Certified Remodelers, Rich is also a Certified Remodeling Project Manager, and three more team members hold the Certified Lead Carpenter credential.
- **A warranty you can read**: Every remodel carries a one-year workmanship warranty covering labor, materials and subcontractor work, and Sweeney transfers manufacturer warranties on products and equipment to you when the job is done.

### Tim Sweeney and the team behind the Sweeney name
Tim Sweeney, CR, is President and Project Developer of Sweeney Design Remodel, a Madison company that began in 1954 as a people-centered business. Linda Sweeney is Vice President and Design Consultant. NARI of Madison gave Tim its Image Award in 2006 and again in 2013. The team today includes project developers, an interior designer, a field production manager, an estimator, lead carpenters, carpenters, a painter and an apprentice. ### From a 30-minute call to a warrantied finish
1. **Phone call and home visit**: A 30-minute call covers your needs, budget and timeline. If it fits, a project developer visits to study your space, existing conditions and scope.
2. **Design agreement and budget analysis**: You sign a design agreement and receive a Comparative Remodeling Analysis, a realistic line-by-line budget based on Sweeney's historical project data.
3. **Design development and trade walk-through**: Designers measure, photograph and draw your plans and guide your selections. Then subcontractors and vendors walk your home to head off surprises.
4. **Pre-construction**: Estimators turn drawings and selections into a contract. Sweeney pulls permits, orders materials, builds the schedule and introduces your lead carpenter.
5. **Construction and warranty**: Your project coordinator and lead carpenter run the job with the trades, and the finished work is backed by the one-year workmanship warranty.

### Questions Madison homeowners ask Sweeney
- **Do I need to move out during a kitchen remodel?** Usually not. Most families stay home, but expect noise, dust and short shutoffs of water, power or gas during demolition and rough-in. Some set up a temporary kitchen with a microwave and small appliances, while others book short-term housing. Your design-build team helps you decide based on scope, utility interruptions and your household schedule.
- **How does the first step work?** It starts with a 30-minute phone call about your needs, what is not working in your space, your budget and your hoped-for timeline. If that conversation lines up, Sweeney schedules a visit to your home to look at existing conditions and scope before any design agreement is signed.
- **What does the one-year warranty cover?** If materials or construction show defects under normal use in the first year after completion, Sweeney repairs or replaces them at no cost to you. The warranty covers labor, materials and workmanship by its subcontractors, and manufacturer warranties on materials and equipment are transferred to you as the manufacturer allows.
- **Why bring subcontractors in during design?** Plumbers, electricians and HVAC partners walk your home with the design team before the contract is priced. They flag issues and suggest options while changes still cost nothing but a redraw, which helps prevent surprises, delays and budget overruns later. Most of these partners have worked with Sweeney for more than 25 years.
- **Is Sweeney the right size for my project?** Sweeney handles kitchens, baths, basements, additions and whole homes, and it has also taken on smaller fixes such as railings, windows and repairs for past clients. One homeowner noted that when a project is too big for the team, Sweeney says so and recommends someone else. A phone consult at (608) 257-3034 settles it quickly.

- **Is there a reward for referring a friend?** Yes, for full-home remodels. ### Before you call: common questions
- **Is the first consultation free?** Yes. Keselman offers a free remodeling consultation. The Estimate Consultant meets you at your home or at the Solon office. You talk through why you are remodeling, set a budget you can stick to, and look at what your home could become. When possible, you also get an approximate estimate based on your ideas.
- **How long does it take to get a full estimate?** Once your design or blueprint is done, the drawings go to suppliers for material pricing while the estimating team writes the labor scope and finish allowances. The process typically takes two weeks or less. The estimate arrives by email, followed by a meeting to review it and make changes before a contract is drawn up.
- **Can I finance a kitchen or bath remodel?** Yes, through Regions Bank on approved credit. Options listed on the site include a 9-month same-as-cash loan, a traditional installment loan from 8.99% to 24.49% APR, and an 11.99% APR loan of up to 12 years. You can pre-qualify online with a soft credit pull. FHA 203k and HomeStyle loan help is also offered.
- **Can I visit your showroom in Solon?** Yes, by appointment. The showroom is at 6500 Davis Industrial Pkwy, Solon, OH 44139, and the office keeps hours Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm. Call (216) 208-6365 to set a time. Many clients pick finishes there with the staff designer during the pre-production stage.
- **Are you insured, and what happens at the end of a job?** The company states it is insured and bonded with each city it works in. Near the end of construction, your project manager walks the home with you and writes a punch list. The touch-up crew then finishes every item on it, and your warranty begins once that list is closed out.

### Why a design studio started its own build company
ARIID Build & Remodel offers design-build remodeling in Kirkland, WA, and it grew out of a design firm. Ariana Adireh Anderson ran Ariana Designs & Interiors for years and kept seeing projects lose their magic between the drawing board and the job site. So she started a construction company with one job: protect the design and build it right.

Today the same team handles the drawings, the city permits and the construction, with the sister design studio choosing finishes and furniture. The firm calls it Design. Build. Furnish. For you, it means one contract, one schedule and one person to call when a question comes up mid-project.

### Design-build remodeling in Kirkland, WA: kitchens, baths and more
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: The team studies where your stove, sink, refrigerator and oven sit today, then looks for dead space in nearby halls, closets or under stairs. Plans cover custom cabinetry and storage, counters, appliance coordination, a layered lighting plan and any structural work.
- **Bathroom Remodeling**: From primary bath overhauls to guest bath refreshes, ARIID handles layout, tile selection, plumbing coordination and construction. Every bathroom gets proper exhaust ventilation to stop moisture and mold, plus storage built in as cabinets, shelves or shower niches.
- **Whole-Home Remodeling**: For homes where the kitchen, primary bath and main floor all need work at once. Designer and builder work as one team, so trades are sequenced together. ARIID plans with you early if you will need to live elsewhere during demolition.
- **Home Additions and New Builds**: Main-floor expansions, second-story additions, ADUs and custom new homes. ARIID handles zoning, building code and HOA review, secures permits, manages inspections and prepares clear estimates covering materials, labor, permits and contingencies, so you see the full cost before construction begins.
- **Aging in Place**: Changes that let you stay home safely without the home looking clinical: grab bars, roll-in or curbless showers, comfort-height fixtures, non-slip floors, lower counters, lever handles, wider doorways and better lighting. It starts with an accessibility assessment of your current layout.

### What you get with ARIID that a builder alone can't offer
- **A designer runs the company**: Founder and CEO Ariana Adireh Anderson is also Head of Design, with over 20 years in the industry. Her sister firm, Ariana Designs & Interiors, picks finishes and furnishings so the build matches the plan.
- **Licensed, accredited and recognized**: ARIID is a Washington State licensed contractor (License #ARIIDBL767NB), BBB accredited with an A+ rating, an NKBA member and a Master Builders Association member, with National NKBA Design Awards in 2021 and 2024.
- **Permits handled for you**: A Google reviewer wrote that permits and code compliance went exactly as outlined at the first meeting. ARIID submits at the earliest design stage and manages the city review through each cycle.
- **Clean, careful crews**: Reviewers mention a crew that kept the work area clean through a basement project while the family lived at home, and a team that showed up on time and cleaned up after itself.

### Meet Ariana Adireh Anderson, founder and Head of Design
Ariana Adireh Anderson founded ARIID Build & Remodel and serves as its CEO and Head of Design. She brings over 20 years of industry experience and still leads Ariana Designs & Interiors, the design studio that ARIID grew out of. The build company exists because she watched good designs get watered down by the time crews built them. Nick Anderson serves as President and oversees operations. Design-build project manager Isabel Valenta guides each job from first consultation to final install through site visits and subcontractor coordination, and customer concierge Line Beaudette keeps scheduling and communication on track.

(Ariana Adireh Anderson, Founder, CEO / Head of Design)

### From first walk-through to final reveal
1. **Site visit and assessment**: The team walks your home, reviews existing conditions and your goals, and checks which parts of the work will need building permits.
2. **Design in 3D**: Designers draw the layout and show it in 3D visualizations, then help you choose cabinetry, tile, fixtures and lighting that fit your budget.
3. **Estimate and permits**: You get a detailed estimate before work starts. ARIID prepares drawings and specifications for permitting and handles the city review.
4. **Construction**: A design-build project manager coordinates subcontractors, visits the site and checks quality against the approved plans, with regular updates to you.
5. **Final walk-through and furnishing**: The project closes with a final walkthrough. If you want it, the sister design studio can furnish and style the finished rooms.

### What Kirkland homeowners ask ARIID before a remodel
- **What does a kitchen remodel cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?** ARIID's kitchen page puts a full Eastside kitchen remodel at about $65,000 to $175,000 or more. Mid-range updates that keep the layout run $65,000 to $95,000. Major changes with a new layout, custom cabinets and premium appliances run $120,000 to $200,000. You get a detailed estimate after a site visit.
- **How long will my kitchen remodel take?** Plan on 3 to 5 months from design kick-off to final walkthrough. Design and permitting take 4 to 6 weeks for standard scopes, and construction runs 6 to 10 weeks. Custom cabinets take 8 to 12 weeks to arrive, so ARIID builds that lead time into the schedule on day one.
- **Do I need a permit to remodel my kitchen?** Yes, if the work touches electrical, moves plumbing, changes structure or adds new vent openings. New counters, refinished cabinets or appliance swaps usually do not need one. ARIID checks permit needs at the first assessment and manages the whole permit process as part of its design-build scope.
- **Will we have to move out during a big remodel?** It depends on scope. When the kitchen and primary bathroom are torn out at the same time, clients usually live elsewhere for 6 to 10 weeks. ARIID talks through relocation planning at kick-off and orders the construction so the stretch when your home is unlivable stays as short as possible.
- **Can you make a bathroom safer for aging in place?** Yes. ARIID installs grab bars, roll-in showers, walk-in tubs, comfort-height fixtures and non-slip floors. A bathroom conversion with a curbless shower, grab bars and ADA-height fixtures typically runs $35,000 to $75,000 on the Eastside. Grab bars in existing tile need no permit, but structural changes do.

### Kitchen and bath remodeling in Warwick, built on 37 years of Rhode Island homes
RIKB Design Build has handled kitchen and bath remodeling in Warwick since it opened its doors in 1989. The family-owned firm plans, designs and installs every project itself, which gives it tighter control over scheduling, quality and cost than a contractor who hands off parts of the job.

### Rooms the RIKB team plans and builds
- **Kitchens**: Simple cosmetic updates, pull-and-replace kitchens or a fully custom room, in traditional, contemporary or modern styles. Designers work on the layout, storage and countertop choice first, because those small decisions often make the biggest daily difference.
- **Bathrooms**: Primary baths, guest baths and closets turned into powder rooms. The designers ask questions you may not have thought of, then help you choose materials that fit your budget, from a simple cosmetic refresh to a spa-like retreat.
- **Aging in Place**: Certified Aging in Place Specialists plan baths and kitchens that work as your needs change, such as zero-entry showers and fold-down shower seats. RIKB has also won a Qualified Remodeler Master Design Bronze award for an accessible bathroom.
- **Additions, Basements and Whole Homes**: Home additions, finished basements, multi-room renovations, game rooms and bar areas. RIKB won a Chrysalis regional award for an addition under $250k and a PRO New England Gold award for an entire house, so larger projects are routine here.
- **Mudrooms, Pantries and Built-ins**: The smaller rooms that make a house run: mudrooms, laundry rooms, pantries, home offices, built-ins and coffee bars. Each one gets the same design consultant, 3D planning and installation crew as a full kitchen remodel would.

### What you get with a Warwick firm that has done this since 1989
- **A five-year guarantee**: Every project is covered by RIKB's Quality Assurance and Five-Year Workmanship Warranty, on top of the manufacturer warranties that come with many of the products installed.

Tanya Donahue is Owner and President of RIKB Design Build, the family-owned company that started in Warwick in 1989 as Rhode Island Kitchen & Bath. ### Bathroom remodel questions we hear in San Antonio
- **How many weeks will my bathroom be out of service?** Most San Antonio bathroom remodels take two to four weeks. A typical mid-range job moves through demolition, rough-in plumbing and electrical, waterproofing and tile, then lighting, mirrors, hardware and a final quality check. Larger or custom bathrooms can take longer, and you get a clear timeline during planning.
- **What does a bathroom remodel cost with C&S?** C&S publishes its ranges: about $8,000 to $15,000 for budget updates like a new vanity, toilet and lighting, $15,000 to $35,000 for mid-range remodels with new tile and a custom vanity, and beyond $35,000 for luxury rebuilds. Every project starts with a detailed written estimate and a complimentary 3D rendering.
- **Do you offer financing?** Yes. C&S partners with several financing providers to offer flexible payment options for bathroom and kitchen remodels. Ask about current terms during your free consultation, and the team will help you find a plan that fits your budget before any work is scheduled.
- **Can you fix mold or water damage during a remodel?** Yes, and a remodel is the right time to do it. C&S works with licensed remediation specialists when needed, then installs moisture barriers and ventilation correctly so the problem does not come back. San Antonio's humidity makes careful waterproofing especially important behind shower walls.
- **Are the 3D renderings really included?** Yes. Every remodeling project includes complimentary 3D renderings at no added cost. They let you compare layouts, materials and features before construction starts and give you, the designer and the crew one shared picture to work from. Detailed selections still come later, but the big decisions get made on screen.

Craftsman Design and Renovation designs and builds kitchens and baths that fit 1900s bungalows, Tudors and foursquares, keeping the woodwork and trim that made you buy the house.

Hero image: https://www.craftsmandesign.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/1902-NW-Craftsman-Kitchen-8.jpg (alt: Kitchen remodeling Portland: 1902 NW Craftsman kitchen with stained wood lower cabinets, soapstone peninsula, white uppers and original-style fir trim)

### Old house nerds with a design-build plan
Kitchen remodeling in Portland gets tricky when the house is a hundred years old. Rooms are small, walls hide surprises, and the trim is worth saving. Craftsman Design and Renovation has spent over 25 years on exactly these homes, from Laurelhurst bungalows to a 1940 Tudor near Mt Tabor.

The team calls itself a group of old house nerds who geek out on original woodwork and the perfect rafter tail. On a 1902 kitchen in Northwest Portland, they replicated stained wood, v-groove wainscot and leaded glass transoms, then set a soapstone counter at the center. The goal on every job is the same: a room that works for today and looks like it was always there.

### Kitchen remodeling in Portland, plus baths, basements and additions
- **Kitchen Remodels**: After a design agreement, the designers draft concept drawings so you can see the layout and how your budget is spent before building starts. Most kitchens include custom cabinetry and shelving, new counters and flooring, a decorative backsplash, and new overhead and task lighting.
- **Bathroom Remodels**: New fixtures, glass shower enclosures, vanities and counters, custom cabinetry, flooring, lighting, and upgrades to ventilation and plumbing. The team drafts the plans, sources unusual materials when a period look calls for them, and handles the carpentry and finish work itself.
- **Whole House Remodels**: A study of your home and nearby houses from the same era guides the design, so every room reads as one whole. Work can happen all at once or in phases, with each phase planned so it sets up the next.
- **Basement Remodels**: Turn a laundry and storage level into a family room, office, guest suite, wine cellar or extra bathroom. The design keeps the new space in step with the rest of your older home while adding the square footage you need.
- **Additions and Exteriors**: Bump-outs, sunrooms, porches, garages and full additions designed to look original to the house, with siding, trim and rooflines matched to the era. Award-winning examples include a 1935 Tudor Revival sunroom and a 1906 Craftsman addition.

### Proof from the trade and from neighbors
- **A long run of NARI awards**: NARI Contractor of the Year awards for kitchens in 2015, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2023, and the 2025 NARI Remodeler of the Year for the 1911 Modern English Kitchen.
- **Fixed-cost construction agreement**: Selections, drawings and the Health and Safety Plan are approved before you sign a fixed-cost construction agreement, so the price is set before the crew arrives.
- **Lead carpenter you talk to weekly**: Your lead carpenter meets with you each week on status and schedule. The work area is sealed off from the house and left broom clean every day.
- **Guildmaster for service**: Guild Quality named the firm a Guildmaster in 2017 and every year from 2019 to 2023, based on client surveys about service.

### From an attic office to SE 27th Avenue
Wade Frietag started Craftsman Design and Renovation in the attic of his 1905 Craftsman home, out of a love for Portland's historic houses. The firm moved to SE Division Street in 2004, above Rejuvenation on SE Grand in 2012, and to SE Belmont in 2015. Today Bill Myles, a Certified Remodeler, owns the company. His team includes designers Erika Rice and Stephanie Capretto, both CKBD, project manager Ryan Murphy and lead carpenters Pete Kelly and Nathan Maszy, both CLC. Clients have called them forensic architects for the way they read an old house.

(Bill Myles, Owner, CR (Certified Remodeler))

### Four phases from first visit to final walk-through
1. **We partner**: An in-home or online consultation, then a flexible design retainer with a realistic target budget and an on-site survey with measuring and photos.
2. **We design**: Floor plans and 3D drawings, then early fixture and finish picks, a detailed scope of work and a preliminary estimate.
3. **We prepare**: A fixed-cost construction agreement, permit drawings with any needed engineering, and a prestart meeting with your project manager and lead carpenter.
4. **We build**: The work zone is sealed off to limit dust and noise, cleaned to broom clean daily, and reviewed with you at weekly meetings.

A flexible design retainer and a realistic target budget come first, then a preliminary estimate during design and a fixed-cost construction agreement before building starts.

### Common questions about remodeling with ELITE
- **Will I be juggling a designer and a builder on my own?** No. ELITE's in-house team covers design, materials, project management and construction. A single ELITE contact guides you from the opening sketch through the last cleanup, so there is no chasing separate trades or passing messages between a designer and a builder.
- **Is REFRESH by ELITE or a full remodel right for me?** REFRESH covers cosmetic and finish-level work like new counters, backsplashes, vanities or a tub-to-shower conversion. If your project moves walls, changes the layout, adds square footage or needs construction drawings, a full design-build remodel is the better fit. Schedule a consultation and the team will tell you which one.
- **What warranty comes with the work?** ELITE provides a 5-year craftsmanship warranty. It applies to full design-build remodels and to smaller REFRESH projects alike. - **Will my remodel stay on budget?** Staying on budget is the point clients raise most in their testimonials. Kitchens in Summerland, on the Riviera and in Rancho Embarcadero came in on budget, and one owner said there were no surprises. Planning and buying materials before demolition is a big part of how the team keeps costs steady.

### Kitchen Remodeling in Homewood, Designed and Built Under One Roof
ELM Construction has handled kitchen remodeling in Homewood and the Over the Mountain towns since 2008. The firm is design-build: the same company draws your plans, picks finishes with you, checks your wiring and plumbing with its trade partners, and runs construction. One team, one plan, one contract.

That setup changes how pricing works. After the design and selections phase, ELM hands you a contract with a detailed scope of work and a guaranteed fixed price, so the big decisions are made before demolition. Hank P. put it simply after his master bath: they stayed on schedule and on budget.

### Kitchens, Baths and the Rest of the House
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Full kitchen gut and redesign, often taking down walls or borrowing space from a dining room. ELM's designers plan stone and quartz counters, built-in professional appliances, custom storage and lighting. Past kitchens include Vestavia, Hoover, Mountain Brook, Cahaba Heights and Edgewood projects.
- **Bathroom Renovations**: Primary suites, guest baths, Jack and Jill baths and small-bath makeovers. Projects range from heated floors and freestanding soaking tubs to custom tiled showers and wet rooms. Plumbing can be moved to fit the room you want, not the one the builder left you.
- **Basement Finishing**: Unfinished or dated basements turned into living space: guest suites, home offices, gyms or a lower-level kitchen. ELM handles water management when needed, new framing, insulation, air conditioning, a bathroom and new flooring, so the space stays dry and usable year round.
- **Additions and Outdoor Living**: Upstairs additions, covered porches and outdoor rooms tied into your existing roofline. Recent work includes a Hoover porch with a stacked stone fireplace and outdoor kitchen. ELM also takes on whole-home renovations and restoration work, including fire damage repair.

### Why Homewood Homeowners Hire ELM
- **A guaranteed fixed price**: Design and detail come first. Trade partners check your electrical, plumbing and structure, then you sign a contract with a detailed scope and a guaranteed fixed price.
- **Two years of written coverage**: ELM backs its work with a written warranty that covers you for two years, which the company notes is double the industry standard.
- **Certified kitchen and bath design**: Designer Liz Kennedy holds the Certified Kitchen and Bath Designer (CKBD) credential from NKBA. Reviewers name her for helping them make decisions without feeling overwhelmed by choices.
- **Your project online, 24/7**: Every client gets an online job portal with the construction schedule, contracts, payment history, change orders and progress photos, open around the clock.

### Elliott Pike, Homewood High Grad and Founder
Elliott Pike and his wife, LeArden, started ELM Construction in 2008. The company prospered through the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression, growing mostly through referrals and repeat clients. Elliott graduated from Homewood High School and Troy University, then worked for a firm that remodeled apartment complexes and a national building materials distributor. He was named the 2023 NAHB Remodeler of the Year and is the 2026 Chair of NAHB Remodelers. He still oversees day-to-day operations, alongside production manager Adam Martz, who joined in 2011.

(Elliott Pike, Founder)

### ELM's Four-Step Design-Build Process
1. **Let's Talk**: Call (205) 273-2773 or fill in the contact form to tell the ELM team about the kitchen, bath or addition you have in mind.
2. **Let's Meet**: A one to two hour discovery meeting in your home, with a real talk about cost and timeline. Everyone with a say should attend.
3. **Let's Design and Plan**: Your space is measured into Chief Architect for floor plans, elevations and 3D renderings, then selections with the designer and a fixed-price contract.
4. **Let's Renovate**: ELM sets the construction schedule, applies for building permits, confirms timing with trade partners and starts work.

### Where the designer and the builder share a last name
Elite Kitchen & Bath has offered luxury kitchen remodeling in Manhasset and across Long Island's North Shore since 1984. It is a design-build firm and a licensed, insured general contractor, so design, engineering, permits, construction and installation all run through one team and one point of contact.

That team is still a family. Yeheskel Sharbani, an electrical engineer, started the company. His son David grew up on its job sites and now leads it as president. Most work comes from referrals and repeat clients, and the owners stay involved in every project, from a new quartz countertop to a full gut kitchen.

### Kitchens, baths and whole homes, designed and built in-house
- **Luxury Kitchen Design-Build**: Space planning, custom or semi-custom cabinetry, stone counters, appliance integration and lighting design, then construction by the same team. Popular requests include large entertaining islands, walk-in pantries, coffee and beverage stations and smart home features. The firm also designs Kosher kitchens and chef-style cooking spaces.
- **Primary Bathrooms**: Spa-style primary baths with curbless and steam showers, large-format tile, skylights and wall-hung Italian vanities. Elite handles the plumbing, tile and glass as well as the design, and several of its Great Neck master baths were full extensions of the home rather than simple updates.
- **Custom and Imported Cabinetry**: American and European cabinetry, including RUTT and Italian lines, plus appliances and finishes from partner manufacturers. Cabinet choices range from semi-custom to fully custom and imported luxury. Built-in wall units, hutches and bars are designed to the inch, and Elite won a Cesar Italian Cabinetry award for outstanding design.
- **Whole-Home, Co-op and Extension Renovations**: Full-home remodels, Manhattan co-op apartments, extensions and interior and exterior work, all managed from the Manhasset office. Elite coordinates filing, zoning and permits in-house. Clients have stayed in their apartments during major remodels while the crew kept the work area neat.

### What North Shore homeowners get with the Sharbani family
- **Owners on every job**: The firm has been family owned for over 40 years and lists owner involvement on every project. Reviewers mention Dave Sharbani and designer Robin Dasilva by name.
- **Award-winning design**: Elite has won 9 NARI Contractor of the Year awards since 2014, PRO Platinum and Gold awards in New York, and David Sharbani was the 2024 Kitchen & Bath Design News Innovator of the Year.
- **Prices published up front**: The site posts real ranges for Long Island kitchens, from $35,000 for a cosmetic update to $300,000 and up for estate-level work, so you can plan before the first meeting.
- **Small jobs get the same care**: One Google reviewer had only a quartz countertop and subway tile backsplash installed and called the work exceptional. The owners replied that they treat all jobs, large and small, with care.

### Two generations of Sharbanis in Manhasset
Yeheskel Sharbani worked as an electrical engineer in a nuclear power plant before founding the company in 1984. His rule was to do it right the first time. His son, David Sharbani, started working for him as a teenager, has spent over 38 years in design and remodeling, and is now president. David's mother, born in France, gave him his love of fine design. Today David's team starts each kitchen by asking how you use the room now and how you want to use it. The team speaks English, Hebrew, Chinese, French and Polish.

(David Sharbani, President; son of founder Yeheskel Sharbani)

### How luxury kitchen remodeling in Manhasset works, step by step
1. **Discovery consultation**: A complimentary meeting about your goals, how you cook and entertain, your style and your investment range. Bring inspiration photos and rough measurements.
2. **Design and planning**: Your designer measures, then develops layouts, cabinet plans and finish choices. Appliances are chosen early because their sizes shape the cabinetry.
3. **Showroom selections**: You review cabinetry, counters, fixtures and hardware in the Manhasset showroom. A design retainer is often applied toward your cabinet purchase.
4. **Construction and installation**: Once drawings are approved, cabinets are ordered with a deposit and Express Contracting handles permits, construction and installation with one point of contact.
5. **Final walkthrough**: Before completion the team walks the project with you to confirm every element meets its standards and your expectations.

### Lake Worth Beach bathroom questions, answered
- **Is the estimate free?** Yes. H&H offers a free in-home estimate with no obligation. The team walks the bathroom, measures it and talks through what is not working. You then get a written scope and a fixed price, set after selections are made, so the number does not creep up through allowances once work starts.
- **My house is in a historic district. Can I still remodel the bathroom?** Usually yes. Lake Worth Beach has six local historic districts, and the city requires a Certificate of Appropriateness before exterior work. A bathroom is interior, so most projects skip that step. If your plan changes a window or an exterior door, or vents through an outside wall, review applies and H&H builds it into the schedule.
- **Florida changed the permit law. Do I still need a permit?** Most likely. Under Florida House Bill 803, some residential projects under $7,500 may qualify for a permit exemption from July 1, 2026, but the city says it is not automatic and owners must apply first. A full bathroom renovation usually costs well above that, and H&H handles the permitting process either way.
- **Do you take small repair jobs?** No. H&H does full renovations only: primary baths, guest baths, powder rooms, tub-to-shower conversions, kitchens, closets and built-ins. Small repairs, maintenance and urgent repair calls are not offered, which keeps the crew focused on the projects it has scheduled and on finishing them well.
- **Can you work in my condo building?** Yes. H&H is insured in Florida and sends certificates naming your association or property manager on request. The team prepares the approval packet, reserves the service elevator and plans work around building hours. Shared waste stacks can limit how far a wet wall can move, so that gets checked at the first walkthrough.

### An East Bay team that plans every detail before demo day
HDR Remodeling has handled kitchen remodeling in Berkeley, Oakland and the nearby East Bay since 1987. The firm's architect, designers, estimator, project managers and carpenters all work for HDR, so the people who draw your kitchen are the people who build it. Many of the homes it works on are older, and the team aims to add modern function without losing their character.

HDR's process is built to keep the build short. Materials are ordered after you sign, and construction does not begin until every item is on the job site and inspected. A lead carpenter is on site each day, and the head of production checks in about every other day and every Friday.

### Kitchen remodeling in Berkeley, plus baths, ADUs and whole homes
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Custom kitchens planned around how you cook and gather, from galley kitchens in Berkeley bungalows to open kitchens with islands in Oakland. HDR's NARI award list includes Regional Contractor of the Year kitchen wins in 2020 and 2023.
- **Bathroom Remodeling**: Primary baths, guest baths and new bathrooms added where none existed. Designers handle tile, vanities and fixtures, and the build team installs them to the approved plans. Recent baths range from Berkeley and Albany to Piedmont, Oakland and Kensington.
- **Whole-Home and Historic Remodels**: Kitchen, dining, living and bedroom remodels that open older floor plans while keeping original details. The design team specializes in historic Bay Area homes and works with an in-house California licensed architect to solve technically challenging layouts.
- **ADUs and Garage Conversions**: Backyard ADUs, studio offices and garage conversions planned with HDR's in-house architect, designers and builders. HDR won a Chrysalis Award for an ADU in 2019, and a recent blog post covers a Berkeley garage turned into a multi-use room.
- **Basements, Attics and Outdoor Living**: Unused basements and attics turned into living space, plus decks, patios and outdoor kitchens from HDR's landscape design-build team. Each one follows the same design, permit and build steps HDR uses for a kitchen or bath.

### How HDR keeps East Bay remodels on track
- **No start until materials arrive**: HDR orders materials once you sign and does not begin construction until every item is on the job site and inspected, so you are not living in a construction zone any longer than needed.
- **Someone on site every day**: Your Lead Carpenter is on site daily unless you are told otherwise. The Head of Production reviews progress about every other day and always on Friday, and you get weekly progress reports.
- **A long record of NARI awards**: The awards page lists NARI Regional Contractor of the Year wins for kitchens and baths in 2020 and 2023, an addition in 2024, a Chrysalis Award and a GuildQuality Guildmaster with Distinction.
- **A warranty past the industry standard**: HDR's Peace of Mind warranty coverage extends well beyond the industry-standard warranty period, and every job ends with a thorough walkthrough before you sign off.

### Led by President Chris Fellows
Chris Fellows is President of HDR Remodeling and has been with the company since 2009. He brings 25 years of construction experience and holds California B General Building and C-6 Cabinet and Finish Carpentry licenses. He is a NARI Certified Remodeling Project Manager, Lead R&R certified and C2 asbestos safety certified. Chris directs HDR's trades, vendors and suppliers alongside Vice President Kevin Mond, who is usually the first person new clients meet. ### The HDR start-to-finish process
1. **In-home consultation**: A complimentary visit to review your wish list and walk the project. HDR suggests starting a Houzz ideabook to share the looks you like.
2. **Studio meeting**: A complimentary meeting at the office and design studio to explore options and estimated cost ranges, and sign a design agreement if you both agree.

### The Premier six-step design-build process
1. **Complimentary consultation**: A one-hour meeting with a designer, usually in the showroom, about your goals, style and budget window. Call, Zoom or in person.

4. **Contract and production**: You sign the construction agreement, meet your project manager at an in-home review, and the build begins with regular site visits.

### Kitchen remodel questions from Kansas City homeowners
- **What is the difference between a kitchen remodel and a renovation?** A renovation updates what is already there, such as cabinets, counters, flooring or appliances, without changing the layout. A remodel changes the layout itself by removing walls or moving plumbing and electrical. Renovating KC offers both and helps you pick the approach that fits your goals, budget and the way your family uses the room.
- **What budget should I plan for?** The kitchen and bathroom inquiry form starts at a $25,001 to $50,000 budget band, and the general consultation form starts at $50,001, with bands up to $500,000 and more for whole homes. Share your range when you reach out, and the team will build the scope of work and preliminary estimate around it.
- **Can we stay in the house during the work?** For basement finishing, yes: most homeowners keep living at home while the crew works efficiently and keeps the area clean. On bigger jobs it depends on scope. One client family lived in the house for the last couple of months of a near-complete gut remodel and said the crew was friendly and respectful the whole time.
- **What warranty comes with a project?** Every completed Renovating KC project includes a full 12-month warranty. It is the final step of the same process that starts with your consultation and runs through design and construction, and the company states plainly that it stands behind its work. Ask your project manager to walk you through what it covers.
- **Which areas do you serve?** Renovating KC works across the greater Kansas City metro from its Lenexa office, including Overland Park, Leawood, Olathe, Shawnee, Prairie Village and Mission Hills in Kansas and Brookside, Waldo, Lee's Summit, Liberty and Independence in Missouri. ### Bathroom remodeling questions we hear in Cary
- **How many days will we be without the bathroom?** The process page lists 12 to 14 business days for installation, including all inspections. Frameless shower glass is custom cut after tile is set and goes in about three weeks later. Your exact schedule depends on scope and product availability, and it is confirmed in writing before work begins.
- **What does the first visit cost me?** Nothing. The first in-home visit, the first showroom appointment and a complimentary remodeling estimate are all free. If you need more extensive design consultations beyond those steps, the site says a consultation fee may apply, so ask about it at your first meeting.
- **What affects the cost of a bathroom remodel?** Room size is only one factor. Moving the layout, the amount of plumbing and electrical work, cabinetry, tile and fixture choices all change the estimate. The team suggests listing your must-have changes first, then comparing alternatives together before you approve the scope.
- **Can you design a bathroom for aging in place?** Yes. Options include low-threshold or walk-in showers in place of a tub, room for a shower chair, a handheld showerhead and grab bars that match the other fixtures. Raise access needs early so entry design, clearances and fixture placement are part of the plan, not an add-on.
- **What should I bring to the showroom?** Bring photos of your current bathroom, rough room measurements if you have them, a list of priorities and pictures of styles you like. Mention whether easy access, storage, cleaning or keeping a bathtub matters most. Those details let the designer make the visit about your house.

### Before you plan a South Shore remodel
- **Is the first showroom visit really free?** Yes. Your first showroom visit and conversation cost nothing and carry no obligation, and the in-home measure and first design and budget meeting are free too. You pay a 5% design deposit only when you sign the design agreement, so you see a full estimate before any real commitment.
- **How far ahead should I start planning a kitchen?** Transitions recommends reaching out 2 to 3 months before your ideal start date. Design, material selection and ordering all take time, and cabinets and other materials can have long lead times. Starting early makes for a smoother schedule once construction begins.
- **Do I need an appointment to visit the Norwell showroom?** No. Walk-ins are welcome Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 5:00 pm and Saturday 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. Booking ahead just makes sure a designer is free to give you full attention. After you send the online form, you can pick a showroom time right away.
- **Can I buy cabinets only and use my own contractor?** Yes. With the materials-only service, Transitions designs the kitchen, selects and orders cabinetry, countertops and hardware, inspects them and delivers to your home. You or your contractor install. A materials-and-installation option adds installation by the Transitions team without the full remodel.
- **Do you build additions with a kitchen or bath?** Smaller additions and bump-outs, yes, especially when they support a kitchen or bath layout already being remodeled. A Marshfield family moved its pantry and laundry into a new rear addition to bring light into the kitchen. Larger additions are taken case by case, usually as part of a bigger remodel.

### Renovation without the runaround
Wright's Renovations offers design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, Ypsilanti and four more Southeast Michigan counties. Design, permits, construction and finish work stay under one roof. Six specialized crews work out of one shop on Platt Road, and every house gets one project manager from contract to the warranty visit.

The team plans around the age of your house. Pre-1920 homes in the Old West Side bring balloon framing and knob-and-tube wiring. Royal Oak bungalows often need a flush beam to open the kitchen, and 1960s ranches may hide aluminum branch wiring. Those known issues go into the proposal from the start instead of turning up later as change orders.

### Design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, room by room
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Full gut renovations, layout reworks and kitchen additions, starting from $75K. Cabinet orders go in the week you sign selections, so the longest-lead item never holds up the build. Most kitchens take 6 to 10 weeks, and recent ones run from Ann Arbor to Belleville.
- **Bathroom Renovation**: Primary suites, wet rooms and half baths, from $40K. Every shower pan sits on a bonded membrane and gets a flood test before tile goes up. Heated floors are a common add in Michigan. Bathrooms carry a five-year craftsmanship warranty.
- **Basement Finishing**: Family rooms, theaters, in-law suites, wet bars and steam showers, from $70K. Before framing, the crew checks the perimeter drain, the sump and the grade outside. Any basement bedroom gets a code-compliant egress window cut in.
- **Home Additions**: Second-story builds, primary suite additions, ADUs and in-law suites, from $185K, with engineered drawings and full permitting handled. In-law suites with a first-floor bath are the fastest-growing request across all six counties the firm serves.
- **Decks and Outdoor Living**: Composite and hardwood decks, three-season rooms and covered patios, from $45K. Footings go below the frost line, and framing is sized for Michigan snow load rather than for the 70-degree day it was built on.
- **Whole-Home Renovation**: Down-to-studs rebuilds, historic restoration and full-floor reworks, from $350K. Work is phased so families can often stay home. On Craftsman and Victorian houses around Ann Arbor, the crew mills trim profiles to match what is already there.

### Why six-figure clients sign with Wright's
- **A fixed number before the contract**: You get a fixed-scope proposal with line-item materials and labor before you sign. Change orders run under 5%, and most projects close at the original signed number.
- **See it before demolition**: An in-house designer measures your home, builds 3D renderings and sources materials as part of the scope. You see the finished room and every line item before you commit.
- **Daily photos in JobTread**: Your project manager posts site photos to JobTread every day, along with the schedule, documents and invoices. You can check progress from a meeting without making a phone call.
- **A clean, livable house**: Zip-wall dust barriers, ram board floor protection and daily cleanup come on every job. Google reviewers call out the punctual crew and the tidy workspace.

### Started at 19 with one pickup truck
Connor Wright founded Wright's Renovations in 2021 at age 19, with one pickup truck. More than 550 projects later, the company ranked No. 610 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 and No. 2 in Ann Arbor. Connor is still the founder who walks sites and answers the phone. He also says no to a finish that will look dated before the warranty runs out. Will Sujek, Chief Revenue Officer since 2021, runs discovery calls and proposals. Katherine Anderson, Chief Administrative Officer since 2024, handles permits and insurance certificates. Clients name crew leads Charles and Chile and designers MacKenzie and Nick in their reviews.

### Four phases, documented the same way every time
1. **Week 1: Discovery call**: A working call about scope, budget and what the space must do. If your number and wish list do not meet, you hear it then.
2. **Weeks 2 to 3: Design and proposal**: In-home measure, 3D renderings, material selections and a fixed-scope proposal with real numbers, so you see the room and every line item first.
3. **Construction**: Zip walls up, ram board down and daily photos in JobTread. Permits are pulled on every job, and Wright's deals with the building department.
4. **Walkthrough and warranty**: Punch list, final inspection, care guide and warranty packet. Your one-year warranty visit is booked before the last truck leaves the driveway.

### What Ann Arbor homeowners ask before signing
- **What does a kitchen or bathroom remodel cost with Wright's?** The company publishes starting points. Kitchens start from $75K, bathrooms from $40K, basements from $70K, decks and outdoor work from $45K, additions from $185K and whole-home renovations from $350K. Your actual number comes as a fixed-scope proposal with line-item materials and labor after the in-home measure and design phase.
- **How long will my kitchen take?** Wright's lists a 6 to 10 week build timeline for kitchens. Before that, the discovery call happens in week one, and design and the proposal take weeks two and three. Cabinet orders go in the week you sign your selections, so the long-lead item does not hold up the schedule.
- **What happens if you find a problem behind the walls?** When a wall hides something, you get photos, three priced fixes and a recommendation within 24 hours. Known issues for your era of house are written in up front. For example, aluminum branch circuits in mid-1960s to early-1970s homes get pigtailed with approved connectors as a proposal line item, not a change order.
- **My house is in an Ann Arbor historic district. Can you still work on it?** Yes. Exterior changes inside Ann Arbor's historic districts go to the Historic District Commission before the building department, and Wright's budgets four to eight weeks for that review. The team designs to the commission's expectations from the start instead of appealing later, and mills trim to match original profiles on older houses.
- **Will you take a small job, like a door or a drywall patch?** Yes, through Wright's Repairs, a separate division with its own technicians and van under the same builder's license. Repairs are quoted in writing from photos and a short video, with a not-to-exceed ceiling. Each job gets before and after photos and one year on workmanship. It covers about 30 minutes from the Ypsilanti shop.

### Questions to ask Alpha before you remodel
- **Can you turn my tub and shower into a wet room?** Yes. Alpha has converted a shower and tub area into a true wet room with a zero-curb entry. That work involved demolition, framing changes, slab work for the curbless entry, drain relocation, waterproofing, tile, plumbing, electrical, drywall and paint. Curbless designs need this planning up front, so it goes into your written scope.
- **How do you keep a new shower from leaking?** Alpha builds the shower pan to code and flood-tests it, then applies one continuous surface waterproofing system, such as RedGard, to the walls, niche, bench and curb. Tile is set with lasers and long levels. The waterproofing is documented, and the work is backed by a written labor warranty.
- **How should I compare remodeling bids?** Look past the total. A useful proposal states what is included and excluded, who supplies materials, how waterproofing will be done, how hidden conditions are handled and what warranty backs the work. The lowest bid can leave out steps that come back later as change orders.
- **What does a kitchen remodel cost in Midland?** Alpha's kitchen planning guide gives these ranges: semi-custom cabinets about $12,000 to $25,000 or more, custom from about $30,000, and quartz, granite or quartzite at $50 to $100 or more per square foot installed. Set aside 10 to 15 percent for surprises. A full kitchen typically takes 6 to 10 weeks.
- **Can I finance a larger renovation?** You can talk with PrimeLending loan originator Stephanie Hecke about renovation loan programs, where costs may be included in a purchase or refinance mortgage depending on the program. Alpha prepares the construction estimate and project details the lender asks for. PrimeLending makes all credit decisions, and Alpha does not.

### Refinish, reface or remodel: your questions
- **Should I refinish, reface or remodel my kitchen?** If the layout and cabinet structure still work, refinishing or painting gives a new look at a fraction of the cost of new cabinets. Refacing keeps the boxes but adds new doors, drawer fronts and hardware. If the layout itself is the problem, a full remodel with new cabinets and counters makes sense.
- **How is this different from hiring a painter?** CCFF has professional sprayers on staff and sprays in a controlled paint booth, which gives a clean, smooth finish. Over the years the team has tested many products and uses only the paints and stains it trusts for cabinets. It can also swap in new hardware or hinges as part of the job.
- **Will refaced doors match my cabinet frames?** Yes. Many refacing companies add veneers that can peel over time from heat and wear, leaving doors that no longer match. CCFF finishes both the doors and the cabinets with the same paint so they age together, and builds doors and drawer boxes in-house on its CNC machine.
- **Can you work with my own contractor?** Yes. If you already have a third-party contractor or handyman involved, CCFF will gladly work alongside that team. On full projects, a dedicated project manager communicates with you daily and keeps the workspace clean and organized so your home stays livable.
- **Do you come to my part of Atlanta?** Yes, most likely. The team works throughout metro Atlanta from its Marietta shop, including Kennesaw, Roswell, Alpharetta, Woodstock, Canton, Smyrna, Sandy Springs, Buckhead, Dunwoody and Decatur. ### Kitchen remodeling in St. Charles, from the wall out
Aptitude Design & Build does kitchen remodeling in St. Charles and across the St. Louis area from its shop on South 5th Street. Many of their kitchens start with a structural question. On one St. Charles home, the wall between kitchen and family room held up the whole second floor. The crew shored it up, set a new beam, and built an oversized island with a second prep sink where the wall used to be.

Because the builders sit in on design, layout ideas get priced and checked for structure early, not after demolition. That matters in older St. Louis houses, where plaster walls, old wiring and earlier remodels can hide behind the cabinets. Google reviewers describe excellent service, great communication and attention to detail from bid to final walk-through.

### Remodeling services for St. Charles and St. Louis homes
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Custom cabinetry, islands, wall removal and open-concept layouts, walk-in pantries, custom range hoods, coffee bars, lighting and plumbing updates. The team asks first whether your current layout works, so you only pay to move what needs moving. Most kitchens take 8 to 12 weeks of construction.
- **Bathroom Remodeling**: Primary suites, hall baths and guest baths with walk-in showers, frameless glass, soaking tubs, double vanities, heated floors and aging-in-place features. Most St. Louis area bathroom remodels run $15,000 to $80,000 and take 4 to 8 weeks of construction.
- **Basement Remodeling**: Finished lower levels with home theaters, wet bars, guest suites, home gyms, offices and added bathrooms, plus egress windows, insulation and drywall. One wellness basement featured in St. Louis Magazine has a sauna, cold plunge, golf simulator and guest quarters. Most take 6 to 12 weeks.
- **General Home Remodeling**: Whole-home and main-floor renovations, structural wall removal, mudrooms, laundry rooms, home offices, built-ins and second-story additions. Larger projects are planned so trades, schedule and quality control stay with one project manager from start to finish.

### Why homeowners from Ballwin to Ladue pick Aptitude
- **Comfortable with structural work**: Load-bearing walls, new beams, moved plumbing and relocated doorways are routine here. The St. Charles open-concept kitchen required temporary shoring for the whole second floor before the wall came out.
- **Builders in the design meetings**: The people who build your project help plan it, so feasibility, selections and budget are weighed together before work begins instead of being discovered during demolition.
- **Noticed by local press**: Aptitude has been featured in the St. Louis Business Journal, St. Louis Magazine, Ladue News and St. Louis Magazine's Faces of Exceptional Remodeling.

Matt Mierek founded Aptitude and serves as its president.
