### St. Charles remodeling questions, answered
- **Can you take out a wall to open up my kitchen?** Often, yes. On a St. Charles kitchen the wall between kitchen and family room carried the entire second floor. The team temporarily supported the structure, installed a new beam and support system, and turned two closed rooms into one open space with a large island.
- **How long will my kitchen be out of commission?** Most kitchen remodels take about 8 to 12 weeks once construction begins. Keeping the existing footprint usually takes less time than moving plumbing or walls. Design, selections, cabinet ordering and permits happen before demolition, so starting those talks early helps the schedule.
- **What does a bathroom remodel cost around St. Louis?** Aptitude says most bathroom remodels in the St. Louis area range from $15,000 to $80,000. Guest bath updates sit near the low end. Primary baths with custom tile, freestanding tubs, heated floors or expanded layouts need a larger budget. Construction usually takes 4 to 8 weeks.
- **Do you handle permits and inspections?** Yes. Permitting is part of pre-construction planning, and the team manages permits and inspections for projects throughout St. Louis, St. Charles and surrounding communities. Plans, trade scheduling and material orders are coordinated at the same time so work can start cleanly.
- **Can you remodel an older St. Louis home without losing its character?** Yes. Older homes may hide uneven floors, old wiring, plaster walls or earlier renovations, and the team plans for those. ### Ames Kitchen Remodel Questions
- **How long does a countertop replacement take?** After you pick your material and color, the team comes out within about a week to make a digital template so the slab is cut to size. Install is usually about four to five weeks later. A plumber disconnects the sink, and the crew removes your old counter the day before the new one goes in.
- **Which countertop material should I choose?** Laminate is the most budget-friendly but the least durable. Granite resists scratches but needs sealing every year. Quartz is the most popular choice and needs no sealing, though it is not heat resistant. Dekton by Cosentino is heat proof and extremely strong. You can compare all four in the showroom.
- **Can I see materials before I decide?** Yes. That is the point of the showroom at 204 Airport Road in Ames. You can walk through cabinet displays and look through hundreds of countertop samples. - **What can I update if my budget is tight?** Smaller updates still change how a kitchen feels. Under-cabinet lighting can be installed in an afternoon. A Libbie and Grove client wrote that every time they move, they call Custom Kitchens for the renovation. The company's promise has not changed in decades: listen, do it right and do it on time.

### What Custom Kitchens designs and installs
- **Kitchen Renovations**: Full kitchen renovations planned from layout to hardware by a certified designer, then installed by the CKI team from tear-out to final install. - **Bath Renovations**: Primary baths and powder rooms designed with the same care as a kitchen, from vanity cabinetry and tile to fixtures and lighting. ### Planning, design and installation, in that order

Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths has handled kitchen remodeling in Martinsburg, WV and across the Eastern Panhandle since 1995. You start in a 5,000 sq. ft. showroom on Rock Cliff Drive, where you can open cabinet doors, compare countertops and stand at real vanities. Then the in-house team builds it.

### Martinsburg kitchen and bath questions
- **How long does a kitchen remodel take?** The whole process of planning, designing, ordering, scheduling and installing can take 3 to 6 months. Most of that time comes before work begins. Once the project starts, a typical Mountaineer kitchen remodel takes about 2 to 3 weeks. Material choices, the size of the job and its complexity all affect the timing.
- **When can I visit the showroom?** The showroom at 1950 Rock Cliff Dr in Martinsburg is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Saturday and Sunday visits are by appointment only, which helps if you cannot get there during the workday. Call (304) 267-6262 to set a time, or just stop in during the week for ideas.
- **Do you do all the work yourselves?** Yes. Mountaineer's in-house team handles every project from start to finish. On recent kitchens that meant demolition, plumbing changes for a new stove, vent ducting, drywall, cabinet installation, trim, toe-kicks and hardware. On one Harpers Ferry kitchen it also meant the engineering coordination for a load-bearing wall.
- **How do you keep a shower from leaking?** Recent showers are built on Schluter shower pans, with Kerdi waterproofing membrane on the walls before tile goes up. The Reap master bath in Harpers Ferry used a 72-inch Schluter pan with a curbless entry. The Dagg shower in Charles Town used the same system, plus a built-in bench and dual niches.
- **Do you offer financing?** Yes. Mountaineer offers financing through Acorn for customers who would rather not pay the full cost up front. Ask about it when you visit the showroom or call (304) 267-6262. Terms and approval come from the lender, so the team can point you to the application while you plan your kitchen or bath.

Schock Construction and Design has handled kitchen remodeling in Issaquah and across the Eastside for more than 30 years. It is locally owned and operated, works only east of Lake Washington and has completed more than 100 projects there.

A kitchen runs $150,000 to $180,000 before appliances, and every scope item, allowance and selection is settled during design so the bid can be fixed before demo day. Anything truly hidden behind a wall goes through a written change order that you see, price and approve before any work on it begins.

- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Plywood cabinet boxes, 3/4-inch solid wood dovetail drawers and soft-close everything come standard, and range hoods over 300 CFM get the code-required makeup air. ### Fifty years of listening to Walworth County homeowners
Stebnitz Builders has offered kitchen remodeling in Elkhorn and across Walworth County since Stan Stebnitz started the company in 1972. His sons bought it in 1986, and his grandson Chris runs it today from the office at Highways 43 and 67. The firm is best known for lake homes, but it also takes on first-time remodels and small bathroom updates.

The method is careful, not fast. Before any demolition, a Project Development Agreement covers 60 to 120 days of planning where cabinets, quartz tops, fixtures and paint colors are all chosen and priced. You then sign a fixed contract, so the budget does not drift once the crew shows up. A five-year workmanship warranty covers what they built after they leave.

### Kitchen remodeling in Elkhorn and everything around it
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Layout changes that fix the work triangle, islands and opened walls for entertaining, pantries and deep drawers for storage, and new lighting and floors. Your budget is checked early with an Opinion of Probable Cost, then every selection is locked before construction.
- **Bathroom Remodeling**: Primary suite and guest bath updates, plus master bath additions. Expect walk-in showers with custom tile, heated floors, double vanities, soaking tubs and steam showers, with fixes for poor ventilation, tight layouts and aging plumbing worked out before demolition.
- **Aging in Place**: Universal design that does not look clinical: curbless showers, comfort-height toilets, blocking for grab bars, wider doorways, lowered counters and main-floor primary suites and laundry. Past work includes a mid-century bath and a Geneva Landings remodel by the lake.
- **Whole Home Remodeling and Additions**: Full-house resets, lake home renovations and additions that go up or out. The team plans structure, trades and finishes together and uses 3D design and virtual walkthroughs, so the new space reads as one home rather than a series of patches.
- **Lower-Level and Exterior Remodeling**: Lower levels finished as media rooms, gyms or retreats, and exterior work including siding, window replacement, roofing and gutters. Restoration projects repair and update older homes while preserving the historic architecture that gives them their character.

### What three generations of building gets you
- **Five years of workmanship coverage**: Most builders offer one year. Stebnitz covers carpentry, installation, plumbing, electrical and HVAC work, exterior finishes and structural changes for five years after completion.
- **A fixed contract after full planning**: The 60 to 120 day Project Development phase settles every selection and cost first, which is how the firm replaces budget creep with a fixed price.
- **One production manager on your job**: A dedicated production manager coordinates trade partners and keeps your household running. A GuildQuality client wrote that production manager Ryan Hibl always returned calls and followed through.
- **Rooted in Walworth County**: A 34-person team based in Elkhorn that coaches local youth sports, volunteers with Habitat for Humanity and supports the United Way and SMILES.

### Chris Stebnitz and the family business
Stan Stebnitz founded the company in 1972, doing general carpentry and small additions. In 1986 his sons Dave, Gary and Dan bought the business and moved it to Delavan. Dave's son Chris Stebnitz became the third-generation owner, and in 2015 he moved headquarters to Elkhorn to sit in the middle of the county. Chris leads 34 people today, from remodeling consultants and designers to field carpenters and apprentices. The company still runs on three rules from the start: always do what is right, serve others as you expect to be served, and never walk away from a project.

### The parts of a kitchen that matter most, done in-house
Woodsman Kitchens & Floors has offered kitchen remodeling in Jacksonville since 1983, starting as a small cabinetry supplier on the First Coast. The company is not a full-service general contractor. It focuses on design, cabinets, countertops and flooring, and it does those parts itself.

Quartz and granite tops are cut and polished in the company's own Jacksonville warehouse, which keeps quality and lead times in local hands. In September 2023 the business became 100% employee-owned, so the designer, the fabricator and the installer in your home are all part owners. The goal is a custom-looking kitchen without a custom price tag.

- **Flooring**: Hardwood, luxury vinyl plank, laminate and tile for kitchens and living spaces, chosen from the showroom displays and installed by the same company that builds your kitchen. - **Bathroom Vanities and Baths**: Bathroom remodeling and vanities with the same cabinet lines, quartz and granite tops and design help used in kitchens. Bennett Contracting handles kitchen remodeling in Albany, NY and across the Capital Region from its offices, showroom and warehouse at 693 South Pearl Street. Design moved in-house in 2016, when Bennett also became a dealer of cabinets and countertops. Designers, project managers, carpenters and trades now work inside one company, so the team that plans your kitchen is the team that builds it. Estimates come from experienced professionals, not commission-driven salespeople.

### Kitchen remodeling in Albany, NY and the rest of the house
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: In-house designers plan layout, cabinetry, countertops, lighting and appliances, then Bennett's own carpenters and trades build it. - **Bathroom Remodeling**: Full bathroom renovations with tile, vanities, shower enclosures, water-saving fixtures and aging-in-place planning. Bennett's bathrooms have won a Qualified Remodeler Master Design Silver Prize in 2026 for a $75,000 to $100,000 bath, and recent jobs include Delmar, Slingerlands and Saratoga Springs.
- **Additions and Whole-Home Remodeling**: Primary suite additions, family rooms, in-law spaces, expanded kitchens and multi-room remodels, with walls moved and structure reinforced where older homes need it. - **Windows, Doors and Decks**: Replacement windows, entry and patio doors, siding, decks, porches and seasonal rooms. Bennett's vinyl windows are made in the Northeast from American-made parts and carry a lifetime warranty, and installers are trained employees, not piece-rate subcontractors.

### A third-generation family business on South Pearl Street
Dan Bennett opened a plumbing shop in a rented garage in Delmar in 1915. After World War II his sons-in-law grew it into DA Bennett Plumbing & Heating. ### Bennett's five-phase remodeling process
1. **Conversation and evaluation**: Bennett learns about your goals, your home and the scope you have in mind, then sorts out feasibility, priorities and next steps.
2. **Design and planning**: Designers, and engineers where needed, settle layouts and structural details so decisions are made before construction starts, not during it.
3. **Pre-construction and permitting**: The team guides you through permits and scheduling so the project meets local codes before any work begins.
4. **Construction and project management**: A project manager coordinates trades, materials and timelines, and keeps you posted as the work moves forward.
5. **Completion and walkthrough**: You review the finished work together with the team, final details are addressed, and the job closes when it meets expectations.

### A small Columbus team, from first sketch to final walkthrough
Elevate Remodeling is a design-build company offering kitchen remodeling in Columbus, Ohio, along with baths, basements and whole-home work. Owner Michael Freed founded it in 2016. He is a Columbus native and Ohio State graduate who has worked in remodeling since 2012, starting with hands-on construction.

Most remodeling companies pass a project from a salesperson to a designer to a crew of subs. At Elevate, the same small team stays with you from the first conversation to the keys. Clients often mention the communication. One Westerville homeowner wrote that the communication was outstanding from the initial consultation to the final walkthrough.

### Kitchens, baths, basements and Amish-built cabinets
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Full remodels, layout changes and lighter refreshes, from a 1960s Clintonville ranch to an Upper Arlington colonial. Recent kitchens added waterfall islands, white oak shelving and a 36-inch Wolf range. Most Upper Arlington kitchens take six to ten weeks from demo to walkthrough.
- **Amish Custom Cabinetry**: Cabinets are built to order by an Amish cabinet maker in Ohio. They use plywood boxes, solid wood face frames, hand-cut dovetail drawers and soft-close hardware, in maple, oak, mahogany or alder. Any Benjamin Moore or Sherwin-Williams color is available, or a custom stain.
- **Bathroom Remodeling**: Primary suites, hall baths, powder rooms, tub-to-shower conversions and aging-in-place updates. Expect frameless glass, custom tile, heated floors and Amish-made vanities. Most Upper Arlington bathrooms run three to five weeks, depending on the plumbing and tile scope.
- **Basement Finishing**: Family rooms, guest suites, gyms, offices and wet bars. The team handles framing, electrical, egress windows and full bathrooms, including trenching the slab for plumbing. Most basements take 6 to 10 weeks of construction after design and permits.
- **Whole-Home Renovation**: Kitchen, baths, living spaces, flooring, trim and finishes handled as one design by one team. Michael helps you decide which walls can move, where storage belongs and how the house should flow. Work is phased so you can plan around living at home.

- **An exact quote, not a range**: After the consultation, you get a 3D rendering and a real number tied to a real plan. The price changes only if you add scope, with no change-order-later routine.

Laplante Cabinetry has made custom kitchen cabinetry in Gray, ME since 2015. It is a family-owned and operated shop, and the founder is the person who builds your cabinets. ### From new doors to a fully custom kitchen
- **Custom Kitchen Design**: Lead designer Kevin Laplante plans each kitchen around how your family uses it, in modern, traditional or contemporary styles. The work covers functional layout planning, space optimization, appliance integration and material selection, so the design fits both your room and your routine.

- **Kitchen Remodeling and Updates**: Remodels range from cabinet refinishing, through partner Eastern Finish, to new doors and hardware, cabinet modifications and complete custom kitchens. One project turned dated orange oak cabinets into a white kitchen with a granite-topped island.

### Kitchen and bath remodeling in Lake County, IL, and beyond

### From a family garage to an Anaheim cabinet factory
APlus handles kitchen remodeling in Anaheim and across Orange County as a design-build firm, with design, construction and cabinet making under one roof. Every cabinet is built in the company's own facility on East La Palma Avenue, so sizes, finishes and inside storage are made for your room, not picked from a catalog.

The business started when Abraham Tabrizi built cabinets in his garage while his young son Alex handed him tools. It grew into an Irvine workshop and then the Anaheim factory, and Alex now runs it. Google reviewers single out cabinet quality, and one client says cabinets bought 13 years ago still please them today.

### Kitchens, baths and built-ins made to measure
- **Kitchen Remodels**: Full design-build kitchens, from space planning and material selection to demo, plumbing, electrical and install. The designer studies how you cook and gather, then plans the layout, colors and cabinetry around it. A detailed 3D rendering is approved before anything goes into production.
- **Custom Cabinetry**: Kitchen, bath, closet and entertainment center cabinets are engineered and built in the Anaheim factory. Keeping production in-house lets the team control quality from start to finish and offer custom pieces for less than outside shops charge, according to the company.
- **Bathroom Remodels**: Bathrooms planned for the space you have, with custom vanities and storage made in the same shop as the kitchens. The design expert works through layout and materials with you and provides 3D renderings, then the construction team builds it to plan.
- **Complete Home Remodels**: Whole-house projects that tie kitchens, bathrooms, entertainment centers, living spaces, closets and additions into one design and one schedule. A San Clemente client had APlus rebuild the kitchen, baths, entertainment center and built-ins in a single project.

### What sets an APlus kitchen apart
- **You can tour the factory**: Your second meeting is at the Anaheim showroom, where you sit down with the designer and lead contractor and walk through the shop where your cabinets will be built.
- **Designer and builder in one person**: Alex Tabrizi is a general contractor and a certified designer, so the plan you approve is drawn by someone who knows how it will be framed, plumbed and installed.
- **Cabinets that last**: Cabinet quality is the most-tagged topic in APlus's Google reviews. A Laguna Hills client says the custom cabinets are built with old-world craftsmanship and have held up amazingly.
- **Most work comes by referral**: More than half of APlus projects come from referrals, and the company reports that over 98 percent of clients interviewed said they would recommend it to friends and family.

### Meet Alex Tabrizi, second-generation owner
Alex Tabrizi grew up in the business. His father, Abraham, started APlus in an Orange County garage building cabinets, moved it to a small Irvine workshop and later to the Anaheim factory. Alex joined the family company more than 25 years ago and now leads it as a general contractor and certified designer. That dual role lets him plan a kitchen that looks right and builds right. His team includes designers, project managers, plumbers, electricians, cabinet engineers and other trades as needed, all working from the La Palma Avenue facility.

(Alex Tabrizi, Owner, general contractor and certified designer)

### How a remodel moves from your kitchen to our shop and back
1. **In-home meet and greet**: A free visit to your home to take measurements and photos of the existing space and hear what you want.
2. **Showroom and factory visit**: Meet the designer and lead contractor in Anaheim, tour the cabinet factory and start on space planning ideas.
3. **Estimate and contract**: You receive a contract written for your scope of work, listing the services included and their costs.
4. **Space planning and 3D design**: A walkthrough to finalize the layout and materials, then a detailed 3D rendering for your approval.
5. **Production and install**: Your cabinets go into production and a project manager leads the job from demo to completion.

### Kitchen Remodeling in Waukesha, Planned Before It Is Priced
Most homeowners looking at kitchen remodeling in Waukesha want a straight answer on cost. GMH Construction puts its numbers on the site: a standard kitchen remodel runs about $75,000 to $100,000 and up, and a premium remodel about $105,000 to $160,000 and up. Your own price follows a design phase, not a guess.

That design phase is the core of how GMH works. A Design Retainer covers the time with their designers, so the scope, selections and budget are settled before construction. Most projects then move to a fixed-price contract: unless you change the scope or selections, the quoted price does not go up.

### Remodeling Services Across Waukesha County
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Custom cabinets, countertops, islands, layered lighting, flooring and storage. Standard remodels may include minor wall changes and moved fixtures over 12 to 16+ weeks. Premium remodels use higher-end materials and can move walls or windows, over 14 to 18+ weeks.
- **Bathroom Remodeling**: Main baths, primary suites and three-quarter baths with custom cabinetry, showers and tubs, lighting and flooring. Pricing assumes a full gut and remodel, and an interior designer works with you through the whole project. Most baths take 8 to 12 weeks.
- **Basements and Lower Levels**: Full lower-level build-outs with three-quarter bathrooms, wet and dry bars, family rooms and home theaters. Projects include utilities, framing, insulation and flooring. A Hartland lower level features a bar with seating beside a brick fireplace.
- **Additions and Sunrooms**: Room additions, three-season and four-season sunrooms, and whole-house remodels that open up older floor plans. One Delafield family wrote that GMH removed walls and staircases that other bidders called impossible, and rebuilt their entire first floor.
- **Signature Series**: A budget-friendly, semi-custom option for kitchens, baths and basements with little to no structural change. You choose from a curated set of popular materials. Published ranges: kitchens $65,000 to $80,000, main baths $35,000 to $48,000, owner baths $50,000 to $65,000.

### What Sets GMH Apart
- **Owners on your job**: Greg or Dane meets you, plans the project and writes your bid, then stays present at your home through construction. Both are reachable by cell phone.
- **Fixed pricing**: Most projects run on a fixed-price contract. Labor and materials are included, and the price holds unless you change the scope or selections.
- **A Design Center to see it first**: Explore cabinetry, countertops, fixtures and finishes in person with GMH designers, who also work with the production team so the design can actually be built.
- **Clean, connected job sites**: Crews clean up daily, and a client wrote that GMH runs a large HEPA air filter to keep dust out of the house. JobTread keeps schedule, finances and documents in one app.

### Owner-Run for Over 30 Years
GMH Construction, Inc. has been remodeling homes in Southeast Wisconsin for over 30 years and is a licensed general contractor in the state. It is owner-run: Greg Perkins and his co-owner Dane meet homeowners, plan projects, write bids and stay on site through construction. Designers Robin and Audrey lead the design phase, and Julie keeps schedules moving behind the scenes. The firm is an active NARI member and holds an A+ rating with the BBB. Many clients come back; one testimonial describes a kitchen, foyer and family room job as a second remodel with GMH.

(Greg Perkins, Owner)

### How a GMH Project Is Planned and Priced
1. **Consultation at your home**: An owner meets you at home to walk the space, set the scope and explain how pre-construction works.
2. **Design Retainer**: About 2 to 3 weeks later, GMH presents a Design Retainer with the scope, a budget range and estimated designer time.
3. **Design and selections**: Designers guide your choices at the Design Center and finish with a set budget and a detailed scope of work.
4. **Construction contract**: Sign the contract, usually fixed-price, and set your start date. Crews generally work from 7:00 to 4:00.

### Know the number before the walls come down
Upscale Remodeling has handled kitchen remodeling in Ithaca, NY since 1991 as a full-service design-build firm. The same team draws your kitchen and builds it, so the design is priced against real construction costs as it develops, not after.

The firm is open about money. Its pricing page says most Ithaca-area kitchens it completes start at $70,000 and most bathrooms at $40,000. During design you get running estimates, and before construction starts you get a fixed price. Older Ithaca homes bring plaster walls, aging plumbing and knob-and-tube wiring, so those are checked early, before design decisions are locked in.

### What the Upscale team designs and builds
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Custom cabinets, quartz and natural stone counters, fixtures, lighting and storage, chosen in the private Design Studio in Freeville. Projects range from updating a dated layout to opening walls into the dining room. Most kitchens are finished in 8 to 14 weeks from the start of construction.
- **Bathroom Remodeling**: Primary baths and half baths, from a leaking tub replaced with new tile, tub, counter and trim to a full redesign with custom vanities. Christie, a Certified Kitchen & Bath Designer, leads design, and most Ithaca-area bathrooms the firm completes start at $40,000.
- **Basement Renovation and Finishing**: Unfinished basements turned into usable rooms, from entertainment spaces to wet bars, designed and built by the same team as the rest of your house. The firm publishes an honest breakdown of basement remodel costs on its blog, so you can plan the budget before the first meeting.
- **Additions and Renovations**: Sunrooms, three-season rooms, mudrooms and kitchen additions that fit the house you already have. One South Ithaca project paired an addition with a renovation, and a Cayuga Heights home gained a three-season room. All permits, inspections and subcontractor coordination are handled directly.

- **A fixed price before construction**: Free pricing guides show typical starting costs, running estimates follow you through design, and the price is fixed before any building starts. Reviewers call it a quality job at a fair price.

Clar Construction has offered kitchen remodeling in Montpelier, VT and the towns within a half hour since 2004. Dan Clar started the company as its only employee. Today it is a full team of carpenters working out of a shop on Granite Street. They build kitchens, baths, additions, decks and custom cabinetry.

The firm's motto on surprises is simple: 'You like surprises? We don't.' Before construction starts, you and the team settle everything from the floor plan down to the grout color and towel bars, so the price can be fixed. Google reviewers note that while others may charge less, the quality justifies the price.

### Built by Clar's carpenters and shop
- **Kitchen Remodeling**: Kitchens planned around how you cook and gather, in modern, farmhouse, traditional or mixed styles. Everything is mapped out before a single tool is lifted. Cabinetry, counters and lighting plans come together with custom pieces from the shop when the design calls for them.
- **Bathroom Remodeling**: Primary baths, three-quarter baths, half baths and brand-new bathrooms. Walk-in showers, glass doors, tiled floors, heated floors, an added window and more storage are all common requests. One Google reviewer had Clar renovate a 50-year-old bathroom after an earlier window job.
- **Custom Cabinetry and Built-Ins**: In its 2,000 sq. ft. shop, Clar builds kitchen and bath cabinets, vanities with matching mirrors, bookcases, mudroom lockers, benches and closets. Built-ins are made to look like they were always there. One client's bookcase and under-stair drawers did just that.
- **Additions and Sunrooms**: Add a room instead of moving. Clar designs and builds additions, mudrooms and sunrooms lined with airtight, energy-efficient windows that bring in light all year. The same team handles decks and porches made for a Vermont summer.
- **Whole-Home, Historic and Aging-in-Place Work**: Clar began in 2004 with a focus on preserving Vermont's historic buildings, and still takes on full remodels of older homes. Many clients also plan changes that help them stay in their homes through retirement, from safer baths to better layouts.

### Is Clar the right fit for you?
- **A fixed price you can trust**: Every detail is chosen during the Project Development phase, so the contract is a fixed price. If you change goals along the way, the cost of that change is discussed openly first.
- **A lead carpenter you already know**: One of Clar's lead carpenters, someone you meet during planning, runs your job. He or she coordinates the licensed electricians, plumbers and roofers and sends periodic updates.
- **Honest about fit**: Clar says it is not for homeowners chasing the cheapest bid or needing work to start tomorrow. It suits people who care more about doing it right than doing it fast.
- **Pricing alternatives offered**: One longtime client wrote that you always know where you stand expense-wise and are given pricing alternatives. Projects typically range from $25,000 to more than $1 million.

### Dan Clar, from steeples to kitchens
Dan Clar grew up in Rochester, NY and earned a degree in Education. In college he worked for a contractor that restored church steeples. He spent half his time in the millwork shop making parts and the other half hanging 125 feet up in a bosun's chair to install them. That job hooked him on carpentry. In 2004 he started Clar Construction in Montpelier as its only employee. The company now works from the historic National Clothespin Company building on Granite Street, turned into a millwork shop. Dan lives in Montpelier with his family and is trying to figure out how to build a wooden canoe.

(Dan Clar, Owner)

### Four steps from first talk to warranty
1. **Get to know each other**: Call, email or walk into the office. Clar learns your ideas, explains its design-build process and suggests a price range based on similar past projects.
2. **Project Development Agreement**: Through a series of meetings with in-house staff or partner designers, you settle every detail, from the floor plan to the towel bars.
3. **Construction**: Your lead carpenter runs the schedule with insured trade partners and keeps you posted on which trades are coming in the weeks ahead.
4. **Completion and warranty**: Near the end, you meet to list any open items, so they get finished while the crew and tools are still at your house.

### Serving Durham, Chapel Hill, Cary and the Triangle
Ironwood Custom Remodels is based in Durham and works across the Triangle and into the Triad. Its service list covers Durham, Chapel Hill, Carrboro, Hillsborough, Cary, Raleigh, Apex, Morrisville, Creedmoor, Burlington and Greensboro. Recent case studies come from Durham's historic Hope Valley neighborhood, the Cambridge neighborhood in Cary and a classic home in Hurdle Mills. Live close by but not on the list? ### Durham kitchen and bath remodeling questions
- **How much does a kitchen or bath remodel with Ironwood cost?** Ironwood has no set price list. Each project is priced on its own materials, labor and other factors, and the estimate is free. Your first phone consultation covers estimated pricing. For scale, Ironwood's 2026 guide puts spa-style primary bath packages in the Triangle at $45,000 to $150,000 or more.
- **How long does a kitchen remodel take?** It depends on scope. In Ironwood's own case studies, the Legacy Kitchen in Hurdle Mills took 10 to 12 weeks. The Blue Haven kitchen in Hope Valley, which included moving structural walls and new Marvin windows, and the Cambridge kitchen in Cary each took 12 to 16 weeks. Ask Ethan for your own timeline at the consultation.
- **Can we keep living at home during the remodel?** Families have. One Google review describes updating an entire early-90s first floor, removing the dining room and greatly expanding the kitchen while the owners lived in the home with their kids and dogs. Ironwood has also published a guide on phasing a whole-home renovation so you do not have to move out.
- **Can Ironwood build a design from my own kitchen designer?** Yes. The Hurdle Mills homeowners had already finished their design with The Kitchen Specialist and chose Ironwood to build it. On other kitchens, Ironwood partnered with Heather Holcombe Designs in Hope Valley and Chess Kitchen & Interiors in Cary. If you are starting from scratch, design is one of the seven stages of the process.
- **Are you licensed, and who handles the permits?** Ironwood Custom Remodels is a licensed and insured North Carolina contractor. Public permit records list the company as the contractor, for example on a Town of Cary permit issued in August 2026 for a primary bath and kitchen countertop remodel. Ask for the licence number when you book your free estimate.
